question: Why does resuming checkpoint 500 (01_direct_rl_coinflip lineage) for further GRPO training reproducibly destabilize (grad_norm/kl exploding) within a handful of optimizer steps, and can it be fixed?

diagnostics.name: seed_diversity
diagnostics.finding: Two different seeds both blew up within 3-4 steps regardless of LR schedule aggressiveness.

diagnostics.name: entropy_clamp_plus_gentler_warmup
diagnostics.finding: Delayed but did not prevent the blowup (step 7 vs. step 3-4); entropy at the blowup step was unremarkable, arguing against entropy magnitude as the driver.

diagnostics.name: per_token_kl_instrumentation
diagnostics.finding: PPO-style importance ratio proven exactly 1.0 by mathematical construction in this config, not the driver. Blowup traced to specific tokens where the policy drifts into meta-commentary/instructional-preamble content the reference model finds highly improbable. Validated against TRL's own logged kl metric to ~7 significant figures.
diagnostics.bug_caught: recurring_rollout_hashes_across_steps field counted elevated tokens per rollout, not distinct steps per rollout hash; fixed via checkpoint500_kl_evidence_reader.ipynb

diagnostics.name: greedy_decoding_check
diagnostics.finding: 0/200 flagged for the same pattern under deterministic (do_sample=False) decoding, pointing at temperature-sampling variance rather than a latent defect baked into the checkpoint.

diagnostics.name: per_token_kl_clamp_mitigation_v1
diagnostics.finding: Executed on AWS EC2 (g5.xlarge, A10G). Did not survive: hard stop at step 14 (grad_norm=109.5, kl=13.08), one step short of the unclamped instrumentation run's own step-15 stopping point. Clamp mechanism verified correct (TRL's logged kl matched the offline reconstruction exactly) but calibrated too loose to matter: CLAMP_VALUE=10334.09 (8x the raw max of per-token KL across steps classified healthy by a 3x-median rule) was exceeded by only 1 of 23,712 scored tokens.

diagnostics.name: per_token_kl_clamp_recalibration
diagnostics.finding: The v1 baseline (raw max of per-token KL across 'healthy' steps) was a single extreme order statistic inheriting noise from borderline steps. Recomputed by excluding any prior-run step within 2x of that run's own breaker thresholds (grad_norm>=25 or kl>=2.5), then took median + 1.5x IQR (Tukey mild-outlier fence) of the remaining 15,640-value clean pool: baseline=0.1012 vs. the old max-based 1291.76. Full per-token distribution check at v1's failing step (14, all 8 rollouts, 1232 tokens) found the worst token was 78.7% of the step's total KL, but excluding it entirely still left a mean of 4.69 (breaker fires at 5.0) -- not a single clean outlier, a real tail of moderately-elevated tokens too.

diagnostics.name: per_token_kl_clamp_mitigation_v2
diagnostics.finding: Executed on AWS EC2 (g5.xlarge, A10G) with the recalibrated CLAMP_VALUE=0.152. Survived to the full 50-step target: terminal_step=50, hard_stop=null. kl stayed in a healthy 0.005-0.07 range the entire run, never approaching the 5.0 breaker; grad_norm stayed well under the 50.0 breaker throughout. The clamp engaged meaningfully this time: 27.5% of tokens were bounded across the run (vs. 0.02% in v1), including one raw spike of 2,371,240 clamped down to 0.152. kl_reconstruction_verified_against_trl_logged_metric=true -- TRL's own logged metric matches the offline reconstruction exactly.

conclusion: Root mechanism identified: temperature sampling occasionally lands on a token the reference model sharply disfavors -- not a defect in the checkpoint, not an importance-ratio effect. First per-token KL clamp attempt (8x multiplier) did not survive past step 14 -- the clamp was calibrated too loose to meaningfully engage. A recalibrated attempt (1.5x a properly-derived median+IQR baseline, replacing the noise-sensitive raw-max baseline) survived the full 50-step target with kl and grad_norm staying comfortably under both breaker thresholds throughout. Checkpoint 500 is now a viable Stage 4 merge target under this specific mitigation.
next_step: Per the project's pre-registered plan, this was the last hyperparameter-side iteration on this mechanism regardless of outcome. Since it succeeded, work proceeds to 05_self_bootstrapping. Any future Stage 4 merge attempt building on checkpoint 500 should carry this same per-token KL clamp (CLAMP_VALUE derived via the median+1.5xIQR-of-clean-steps method, not the original raw-max method).
